chatThreadBlock.title: Chat Thread
chatThreadBlock.description: Composable streaming conversations with message editing, reply versions, anchored history and checkpoint restoration.
chatThreadBlock.compositionBody: Built on the shared @zeron/ui/chat-thread AI component; existing block exports and demo helpers remain compatible. ChatThread owns one conversation scroller, the message rail and a persistent composer slot. ChatUserMessage and ChatAssistantMessage reuse ChatMessage, whose meta slot owns response metadata layout. InputMessage retains attachments, drafts, Stop and its controlled queue. ThinkingSteps, CodeBlock, CodeDiff, ModelSelector and ContextWindowCompact compose through existing slots. The Floating block surface uses Empty for its default welcome, Separator for rules, InlineNotice for errors and stopped generation, and MessageNavigation for the compact conversation rail. SurfaceProvider passes the Floating level to nested popovers. The empty state retains the same composer node; adding the first message does not remount its editor. Give the block a constrained height, such as h-full inside a flex parent with min-h-0. ChatMessage presents one message; ChatThread and its registered ChatUserMessage / ChatAssistantMessage entries coordinate the conversation. ChatAction, ChatCopy, ChatBranchSwitch, ChatAttachments, ChatEditor and shared type aliases remain exported for compatibility; new compositions use chat-message primitives with explicit labels and disabled state.
chatThreadBlock.usageBody: Install chat-thread and input-message for the shared components. The chat-thread-01 compatibility entry remains available with its original demo-data exports. Install chat-thread-01 and input-message. The composer is a slot; install model-selector-01 and context-window-02 separately when your application needs those controls. Mount one Toaster at application level for restore and undo feedback.
chatThreadBlock.apiMessages: Ordered ChatUserMessage, ChatAssistantMessage and ChatDivider elements. Keep each logical message ID stable across versions and unique within this thread.
chatThreadBlock.apiComposer: The composer stays mounted. empty replaces the default heading above it when no messages are registered.
chatThreadBlock.apiBusy: Marks the conversation busy and disables history-changing message actions while a reply is generated or a mutation is running.
chatThreadBlock.apiOlder: Shows the earlier-history action. Await loading in onLoadOlder, or keep loadingOlder true until prepended messages are committed. Loading disables history-changing message actions and defers undo; restore and undo disable the load action. Rejections preserve the history and show a retryable error.
chatThreadBlock.apiRestore: Receives the checkpoint ID and whether code should be restored. Resolve after committing the host mutation, reject on failure, and optionally return an undo callback. Code restoration requires a real host integration.
chatThreadBlock.apiFocus: Use the same ref with InputMessage.textareaRef. A successful restore focuses the editor with the caret at the end.
chatThreadBlock.apiBookmarks: Controlled bookmarks for logical user-message IDs. Providing onBookmarkChange shows the bookmark toggle in the navigation preview. The callback requests a new state; update bookmarkedIds after the host accepts it. bookmarkLabels localizes its accessible name and tooltip. Storage and failures belong to the host.
chatThreadBlock.apiLabels: Localize actions and announcements with labels, including function labels for counts. locale formats timestamps. English and Chinese label objects are exported.
chatThreadBlock.messagesBody: ChatUserMessage takes id, text, files (( id, name, type?, size?, url? )), attachments, time, pin, branch, checkpoint and onEdit. pin positions the newly sent turn at the top. ChatAssistantMessage takes id, children, plain text for copying, streaming, last, meta, branch, feedback, onFeedback, onRetry, error and stopped. streaming hides actions; last keeps them visible. branch is ( index, count, onChange ), with a zero-based index. ChatMarkdown renders safe GFM and Zeron code blocks; children can instead contain your own reasoning, tool results or rich content. model, modelLogo and provider describe the actual response identity. ChatMessageAuthor shows the logo, medium-weight model name and muted provider above content, including during streaming. metrics takes ttftMs, inputTokens, outputTokens and durationMs; the footer shows metrics without repeating the model before TTFT. Times are milliseconds and token counts are nonnegative integers. Missing or invalid values are omitted. meta adds custom footer metadata. Save model and provider per reply so changing the selector preserves previous responses. Image previews and filenames share one bordered card, for both local files and persisted attachments.
chatThreadBlock.historyBody: The view follows growing replies until the reader scrolls away. Scroll to latest resumes following. Prepending history preserves the visible message and its offset. The desktop rail reuses MessageNavigation: compact lines indicate user turns and the current position, with a left-side preview of the question and the following reply’s first paragraph. Click to jump and focus the turn. Tab enters the rail once; arrows, Home and End move focus; Enter or Space selects; Escape dismisses the preview. Long rails scroll internally, while narrow screens retain the main scroller without the rail. The host retains version history and corresponding descendants; branch arrows request a selection and never overwrite messages themselves. splitThreadHistory(messages, messageId) returns kept and removed arrays, including the selected user message in removed; a missing ID leaves the history intact. The local demo preserves independent continuations for each version.
chatThreadBlock.restoreBody: Checkpoints merge and deduplicate changed file paths across the selected and later turns, and show the affected message count before confirmation, and dim the messages that would be removed. The host removes the selected user message onward and restores its text and attachments into the composer. Pause InputMessage automatic queue release with autoDispatchQueue=false during restores, edits and version switches. Snapshot draft, attachments, queue and conversation together for undo. Failed restores keep the confirmation open; failed undo remains retryable. Invalidate or reject stale undo after later edits to avoid overwriting newer work.
chatThreadBlock.keyboardBody: Tab reveals message actions. Enter sends an edit, Shift+Enter adds a line, and Escape cancels and returns focus to the message. Enter waits during IME composition. The focused conversation accepts native scrolling keys. Restore confirmation uses Popover focus management; Escape returns focus to its trigger and successful restoration focuses the composer. Replies use a labelled log, busy state, feedback pressed states and live announcements. Touch actions remain visible; reduced motion disables message entrance and nonessential transitions.
chatThreadBlock.demoBody: Replay restores the fixture. New chat shows the empty state. Send streams a local reply, Stop keeps the partial text, and messages sent during generation enter the existing queue. Edit and retry create versions; switching versions restores their own continuation. Error example exposes failure and retry. Load earlier messages, checkpoints and undo are interactive. Replies, model data, context compaction and file restoration are simulated; the demo does not contact a model, modify disk files or upload attachments. Response timings are measured from the local simulation; seed metrics and token counts are mock data. Changing the model selector affects future replies only.
